summary: Lajos Ligeti was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös József Collegium, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Paris under Paul Pelliot, Henri Maspero, and Jacques Bacot, later holding posts at Eötvös Loránd University.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under the traditional teachers Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Lakshmanacharya worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Shri Ramanuja Pathashala in Mathura, attested in 1889 and 1900.

Lakshmi Swaminathan worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Queen Mary's College (~1930–1932) and Madras Medical College (~1932–1938), and served as a Retired Lecturer at Stony Brook University.

Lal Mani Joshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Gorakhpur University under Govind Chandra Pande and held posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, Harvard, Haverford, Amherst, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology. He held positions at the Central Library of Vadodara as a Jain Pandit and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1939).

Lama Jabb specializes in Tibetology. He has held positions at the University of Oxford as a Junior Research Fellow and at Wolfson College, Oxford, as Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre (attested 2026).

Lama Jampa Thaye works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester, studied under traditional teachers including Karma Thinley Rinpoche and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and taught at the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ngor E-Vam Choden Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959, and founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

Lama Palden Drolma specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.

Lambert Schmithausen is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker, and held academic posts at the University of Münster (1970–1973) and the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986 and served as a professor at the University of San Diego (attested 1997).

Lance S. Cousins worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and K. R. Norman, and held posts at Manchester, Oxford, Wolfson College, the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies, and the Pali Text Society.
Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Yale University, studying under Koichi Shinohara, Phyllis Granoff, and Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Temple University, where she studied under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Lara Braitstein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and became Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism there (attested 2026).

Larry DeVries works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Minnesota and held teaching or research posts at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Washington, Chicago, and Langara College (attested 2005).

Lars Fogelin specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli, and held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.
Lars Martin Fosse is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Oslo, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn, and taught at the University of Oslo (attested 2002).
